The test image shows a corn ear heavily covered in dark black/sooty mass, with husks partially open revealing dark spore material replacing the kernels. This is an ear/pod affected part.

Top candidates from pod/seed classes: Head_Smut, Common_Smut, Trichoderma_Ear_Rot, Diplodia_Ear_Rot, Gibberella_Disease, Aspergillus_Ear_Rot, Fusarium_Disease, Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight.

Let me view one reference from each top candidate, starting with the most likely.
Head_Smut reference shows dark spore mass inside the husk - similar dark material but the plant is dried/dead. Let me check Common_Smut next.
Common_Smut shows distinctive white/silvery galls - very different from the test image's uniform dark mass. Let me check more candidates.
Trichoderma shows green-gray mold on husks - not matching. Let me check more.
Diplodia shows yellowed ears with white mold - not matching. Let me check Gibberella, Aspergillus, Fusarium, and a second Head_Smut reference.
Gibberella shows pink/red mold on husks - not matching. Let me check Aspergillus and Fusarium.
Aspergillus shows olive-green powdery mold on kernels - not matching. Let me check Fusarium.
Fusarium shows white/pink mold on kernels - not matching. Now let me view a second Head_Smut reference to confirm, since it was the closest match.

This is a strong match. The Head_Smut reference (Corn_Disease_206) shows an ear with husks peeled back revealing a dark black mass of spores inside, very similar to the test image. Both show:
- Husks partially open
- Dark black sooty spore mass replacing the kernels/ear contents
- Green plant still alive around the infected ear

The test image matches Head_Smut closely. The entire ear interior is replaced by dark brown-black teliospores, which is the hallmark of Head_Smut. Common_Smut was ruled out because it shows distinct white/silvery galls rather than a uniform dark mass replacing the whole ear. All other ear rot candidates (Trichoderma, Diplodia, Gibberella, Aspergillus, Fusarium) show colored molds on kernels, not the complete replacement with dark spore mass seen here.
